q: What is the earliest age at which a Texas teen can get a learner license?
exp: A learner license is available from age 15 once the required driver education classroom hours are done.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 1; dps.texas.gov, Texas Learners License as a Teen

q: What score do you need to pass the Texas Class C knowledge test?
exp: Every Texas knowledge exam requires a grade of at least 70 percent.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 7; 37 TAC 15.52 and 15.64

q: Who may supervise a teen driving on a Texas learner license?
a: A licensed driver 18 or older with a year of experience, in front
b: A licensed driver 18 or older with two years of experience, in front
c: A licensed driver 21 or older with a year of experience, in front
d: A licensed driver 21 or older with any experience, in any seat
exp: The supervisor must be a licensed driver 21 or older with a year of experience, sitting beside the learner.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 1

q: How long must a Texas teen hold a learner license before getting a provisional license?
exp: Phase One requires holding a learner or hardship license for at least six months.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 2; dps.texas.gov, Texas Provisional License as a Teen

q: How many hours of supervised behind-the-wheel practice must a Texas teen complete in driver education, and how many at night?
exp: Teen driver education includes 30 hours of supervised practice, with at least 10 of them at night.
src: dps.texas.gov, Texas Provisional License as a Teen; TDLR Parent Taught step by step guide; 16 TAC 84.50

q: With a Texas provisional license, how many passengers under 21 who are not family members may ride with you?
exp: A provisional driver may carry no more than one passenger under 21 who is not a family member.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 3; dps.texas.gov, Texas Provisional License as a Teen

q: During which hours may a Texas provisional license holder not drive, unless an exception applies?
exp: Phase Two drivers may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. except for work, school activities or a medical emergency.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 3

q: When must a Texas teen complete the Impact Texas Teen Drivers (ITTD) program?
a: Before applying for a learner license
b: Within one year before the road test
d: Within 90 days before the road test
exp: The ITTD certificate must be dated within 90 days of the driving test.
src: dps.texas.gov, Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) Program; ITTD FAQ; dps.texas.gov, Texas Provisional License as a Teen

q: A Texas driver under 18 may use a cell phone while driving only:
c: While stopped at a red light
d: When a licensed adult is in the car
exp: Drivers under 18 may not use any wireless device, even hands-free, except in an emergency.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 3

q: During a Texas road test, how many points can you lose before you fail?
a: More than 15 points lost is a fail
b: More than 30 points lost is a fail
c: More than 20 points lost is a fail
d: More than 50 points lost is a fail
exp: An application is not approved if more than 30 points are deducted on the driving exam.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 8

q: Who must complete an approved driver education course to get a first Texas license?
d: Every first-time applicant, at any age
exp: Texas requires driver education for applicants younger than 25; those 25 and older are exempt.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 7; dps.texas.gov, Apply for a Texas Driver License

q: What driver education must an 18-year-old applying for a first Texas license complete?
b: No course, since adults are exempt
d: A six-hour adult driver education course
exp: Applicants 18 through 24 must finish a six-hour adult driver education course.
src: dps.texas.gov, Apply for a Texas Driver License

q: Which Impact Texas Drivers course do applicants 18 and older take before the road test?
d: No course is required for adults
exp: Drivers 18 to 24 completing adult driver education, and drivers 25 and older, take the ITAD video.
src: dps.texas.gov, Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) Program; ITTD FAQ

q: About how long is the Impact Texas Teen Drivers video course?
exp: ITTD is a free video program of about two hours in eight modules.
src: dps.texas.gov, Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) Program; ITTD FAQ

q: What happens if you do not pass the road test within 90 days of finishing ITTD?
b: You must repeat all of driver education
d: You must wait six months to retest
exp: The ITTD certificate expires 90 days after it is issued, so the program must be repeated.
src: dps.texas.gov, Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) Program; ITTD FAQ

q: In what form must you bring your ITTD certificate to the road test?
c: No copy; DPS looks it up
exp: Electronic copies are not accepted; bring the printed certificate.
src: dps.texas.gov, Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) Program; ITTD FAQ

q: How many hours of classroom instruction does Texas teen driver education include?
exp: Teen driver education has 24 classroom hours plus 44 hours of in-car work.
src: dps.texas.gov, Impact Texas Drivers (ITD) Program; ITTD FAQ; TDLR Parent Taught step by step guide; 16 TAC 84.50

q: In a concurrent teen driver education course, after how many classroom hours may you apply for a learner license?
exp: With the concurrent method, a teen may apply after the first 6 classroom hours; a block course requires all 24.
src: dps.texas.gov, Texas Learners License as a Teen

q: Besides 30 hours of practice, how many hours of in-car observation and in-car instruction does Texas teen driver education require?
exp: The in-car phase includes 7 hours of observation and 7 hours of instruction.
src: dps.texas.gov, Texas Provisional License as a Teen; TDLR Parent Taught step by step guide; 16 TAC 84.50

q: What is a Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) form used for?
c: To show the vision test was passed
d: To prove a teen is attending school
exp: Applicants under 18 without a diploma or GED present a VOE signed by the school.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, pp. 1 to 2; dps.texas.gov, Texas Learners License as a Teen

q: During the school year, how long is a VOE form valid after it is issued?
exp: A VOE is valid for 30 days, or 90 days if issued in the summer.
src: dps.texas.gov, Texas Learners License as a Teen

q: Which application form does a Texas applicant under 17 years and 10 months use?
exp: DL-14B is the minor application; DL-14A is for applicants 17 years 10 months or older.
src: dps.texas.gov, Driver License Forms

q: If a parent cannot come to the DPS office with a teen applicant, what must the teen bring?
a: A signed letter from the parent, without a notary
b: A VOE form signed by the school principal
c: The application signed by the parent and notarized
d: A copy of the parent's driver license
exp: A parent or guardian must attend, or the teen brings a notarized application signed by the parent.
src: dps.texas.gov, Texas Learners License as a Teen

q: What does a Texas learner license cost for an applicant under 18?
exp: The under 18 learner license fee is $16, including the $1 administrative fee.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 1; dps.texas.gov, Driver License Fees

q: What does a new eight-year Class C license cost an applicant 18 or older?
exp: The Class C license for ages 18 to 84 is $33, including the $1 administrative fee.
src: dps.texas.gov, Driver License Fees

q: When does a Texas provisional license expire?
a: One year after it is issued
d: Six months after it is issued
exp: The provisional license is marked PROVISIONAL and expires on the 18th birthday.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 3

q: Which is an exception that allows a provisional driver to drive between midnight and 5 a.m.?
a: Driving a friend home from a party
c: Driving to or from a job
exp: Exceptions cover work, school-related activities and medical emergencies.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 3

q: If a Texas learner license is suspended, what happens to the six-month holding period?
a: It starts over from the day the suspension ends
b: It keeps running during the suspension
c: It is extended by a flat 90 days
d: It is extended by the days suspended
exp: The license is invalid during a suspension, so those days are added to the six months.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 2

q: Through a Texas driver education course, the knowledge test is given as:
a: Two exams, signs and rules, each needing 70 percent
b: One combined exam on signs and rules, needing 70 percent
c: Two exams, signs and rules, each needing 80 percent
d: Two exams, signs and rules, averaged to 70 percent
exp: Course providers give separate Class C Road Signs and Road Rules exams, and each must be passed at 70 percent.

q: In which languages are Texas knowledge exams offered?
exp: Written and oral exams are offered in English and Spanish.

q: If you fail an exam at a Texas DPS office, how long does your application stay open?
a: 30 days, or until two failed exams
b: One year, or until five failed exams
c: 90 days, or until three failed exams
d: Until you pass, with no limit
exp: After 90 days or three failed exams, a new application and fee are required.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 7

q: Which four basic skills is every Texas road test applicant graded on?
a: Control, parking, backing and quick stopping
exp: All drivers are graded on control, observation, positioning and signaling.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 8

q: During parallel parking on the Texas road test, which feature may you use?
exp: A backup camera is allowed, but an automated parking function is not.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 8

q: On the Texas road test quick stop, from about what speed are you asked to stop quickly without skidding?
exp: The quick stop is made from about 20 mph without skidding the tires.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 8

q: Where may a Texas teen take the road test?
a: At a DPS office, by appointment, and nowhere else
b: At any licensed driving school, approved or not
c: At DPS or an approved third party testing school
d: At DPS, or with a parent who teaches the course
exp: The non-commercial driving exam may be given by DPS or by a third party skills testing school.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 8; dps.texas.gov, Texas Provisional License as a Teen

q: How long can a new Texas resident drive on a valid license from another state?
exp: New residents may drive on a valid out-of-state license for up to 90 days after moving.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 1; dps.texas.gov, Moving to Texas

q: An adult new resident surrenders a valid license from another state. Which tests must they take in Texas?
a: Neither the knowledge test nor the road test
b: The knowledge test, but not the road test
c: The road test, but not the knowledge test
d: Both the knowledge test and the road test
exp: Adults surrendering a valid out-of-state license are not required to take the knowledge or skills exam.
src: dps.texas.gov, Moving to Texas

q: Which country's license holders can exchange a valid license in Texas without the knowledge and road tests?
exp: Texas has reciprocity with France, Germany, South Korea, Taiwan and the United Arab Emirates.
src: dps.texas.gov, Moving to Texas

q: Before a new resident applies for a Texas license, what must be done with any vehicle they own?
a: Transfer the title only; registration can wait
b: Show it to the examiner at the road test
exp: New residents must show that each vehicle they own is registered in Texas.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 7; dps.texas.gov, Apply for a Texas Driver License

q: What marks a Texas license as REAL ID compliant?
a: The words REAL ID printed across the top
b: A blue star in the lower left corner
c: A hologram of the state capitol building
d: A gold star cutout in the upper right
exp: Texas issues only REAL ID compliant cards, marked with a gold star.
src: TSA press release on Texas REAL ID; KCBD report quoting DPS

q: After you pass all Texas exams, how long is your temporary license valid while the card is mailed?
exp: The temporary license may be used for 45 days or until the permanent license arrives.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 7

q: Within how many days must you report an address change to Texas DPS?
exp: A change of address must be reported to DPS within 30 days.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 9

q: A sign shaped like an octagon always means:
exp: The octagon is used only for stop signs.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: Which sign shape is used only for yield signs?
c: A diamond turned on its point
exp: The triangle shape is reserved for yield signs.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: A sideways triangle shaped like a pennant on the left side of the road warns of:
exp: The pennant gives advance warning of a no-passing zone.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: A five-sided (pentagon) sign is used for:
exp: The pentagon marks school advance and school crossing signs.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: A round yellow sign with an X and RR warns of:
b: A rest area for trucks ahead
exp: The round shape is used for railroad advance warning signs.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, pp. 27, 33

q: A diamond shaped sign tells you:
a: The speed limit for the road ahead
b: The route number of the highway
c: Gas, food and lodging services ahead
d: A hazard or condition is ahead
exp: Diamond signs warn of existing or possible hazards.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: What does an orange sign mean?
b: A general warning of a hazard ahead
c: A park or recreation area ahead
d: Gas, food or other motorist services
exp: Orange is used for construction and maintenance warning signs.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: A brown sign points you to:
exp: Brown signs guide drivers to public recreation and scenic areas.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: A blue sign gives information about:
exp: Blue signs guide drivers to motorist services.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: On a road sign, the color green indicates:
a: A general warning of a hazard ahead
b: An action that is not allowed
exp: Green is used for permitted movements and guide signs.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: A square yellow plaque showing 30 MPH below a curve sign tells you:
a: The highest safe speed for the curve
b: The minimum speed on the curve
c: The speed limit for the next mile
d: The speed limit for trucks only
exp: An advisory speed sign gives the highest speed for safely driving through the curve.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 30

q: You see a red rectangular WRONG WAY sign facing you. What does it mean?
a: The road ahead is closed and you must detour
b: You are driving against the flow of traffic
c: You must turn around at the next exit
d: You must yield to oncoming traffic
exp: It means you are going the wrong way and directly opposing the flow of traffic.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 30

q: A sign reads LEFT LANE FOR PASSING ONLY. What should slower traffic do?
a: Use the far left lane at the speed limit
c: Keep out of the far left lane
d: Use any lane, if at the speed limit
exp: On roads with more than one lane each way, the far left lane is for passing.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 31

q: A center lane marked for left turns in both directions may be used to:
b: Stop to let a passenger out
c: Drive in it for several blocks before turning
d: Slow or stop before turning left
exp: The center lane is only for vehicles turning left, never for passing or through travel.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, pp. 31, 34

q: A sign with arrows over two left lanes says both may turn left. Traffic in the far left lane:
b: May go straight or turn left
exp: In a double left turn, the far left lane must turn left and the other lane has a choice.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 30

q: What does a red X over a lane on an overhead lane-use signal mean?
a: The lane is for buses only
b: Do not drive in that lane
d: The lane ends in one mile
exp: A red X means you should not drive in that lane.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 33

q: A steady yellow X over your lane on a lane-use signal means:
a: Speed up to clear the lane
b: The lane is open for turning only
c: Prepare to leave the lane safely
d: Stop in the lane and wait
exp: A steady yellow X warns that the lane control is changing, so move out of the lane safely.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 33

q: In a work zone, a flagger wearing an orange vest holds up a STOP paddle. What do you do?
a: Slow down and pass the flagger with care
b: Stop, then go once the road looks clear
c: Move to the left lane and continue
d: Stop and wait until the flagger waves you on
exp: A flagger's instructions must be obeyed; stop in your lane and move only when told.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 37

q: Diagonal stripes on a barricade slope down to the right. Which way should you pass it?
exp: Stripes sloping downward to the right mean bear to the right.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 37

q: A large flashing arrow panel in a work zone tells you:
a: Workers are ahead; slow down but keep your lane
b: A lane ahead is closed; merge the way it points
c: An exit ahead; take it in the arrow's direction
d: Traffic may use the shoulder the way it points
exp: Arrow panels guide drivers into open lanes when part of the road is closed.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 37

q: The railroad crossbuck sign marks:
a: Advance warning that tracks are ahead
b: A four-way stop at a crossing
c: Where the tracks cross the road
d: A crossing closed to all traffic
exp: Crossbucks are posted at every grade crossing to show where the tracks are.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 33

q: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, how far from the nearest rail must you stop?
exp: Texas drivers stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail when a train is signaled.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 4, p. 21; Ch. 5, p. 34

q: A sign with yellow lights at the top and bottom flashing before a freeway ramp means:
c: A school zone is in effect
d: The ramp is for trucks only
exp: Flashing lights on this sign show that a ramp meter ahead is in use.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 29

q: What does an ALL WAY plaque under a stop sign mean?
a: Cross traffic does not stop for you
b: Traffic from every direction must stop
c: You may turn right without stopping
d: A signal ahead is out of service
exp: All approaching traffic must stop and proceed in the order of arrival, yielding to the right on a tie.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 31

q: A sign shows a crossed out phone in a school zone. What does it tell you?
a: Phones may be used hands-free only
b: Texting is banned, but calls are allowed
c: Wireless device use is banned in the zone
d: Phones are banned only for drivers under 18
exp: This sign marks a school zone where using a wireless communication device is prohibited.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 31

q: A double solid white line between two lanes means:
b: Lane changes are discouraged but allowed
c: You may cross it to pass slow traffic
d: Do not change lanes across it
exp: Crossing double solid white lines is prohibited.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, pp. 31, 35

q: A vertical rectangle is the shape generally used for:
exp: Vertical rectangles are generally regulatory signs.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: A horizontal rectangle is the shape generally used for:
exp: Horizontal rectangles are generally guide signs.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: A yellow sign means:
b: Services such as gas and food
exp: Yellow is used for general warning signs; orange is for work zones.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 27

q: A yellow sign shows a car with wavy skid marks. What should you do?
a: Brake hard if the car starts to slide
b: Keep your speed but pump the brakes often
c: Pull onto the shoulder until the road dries
d: Slow down and avoid sudden braking or turns
exp: The slippery when wet sign warns you to slow down and avoid sudden moves.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 28

q: A LANE ENDS sign is posted ahead and you are in the lane that ends. You should:
a: Merge into the other lane when safe
b: Stay in your lane and stop where it ends
c: Speed up to pass the other traffic
d: Use the shoulder to get past the merge
exp: Drivers in the ending lane must merge into the lane that continues.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 29

q: A DIVIDED HIGHWAY ENDS sign warns that:
a: A median crossover for U-turns is ahead
b: Two-way traffic without a median begins ahead
exp: The divided highway ends and opposing traffic is no longer separated.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 28

q: A speed sign posted at a highway exit ramp shows:
b: The speed limit on the next road
c: The safe speed for traveling the ramp
exp: An exit speed sign gives the speed at which the ramp may be traveled safely.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 30

q: How often are mileposts placed on Interstate highways?
exp: Mileposts are erected every mile on Interstates to help locate crashes and breakdowns.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 33

q: In a Texas school zone, when does the lower speed on the School Zone sign apply?
a: While its lights flash or during posted hours
b: When you can see children near the road or crosswalk
c: All day on every school day of the year
d: From 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. on school days
exp: The school zone speed is in effect when the yellow light is flashing or at the posted times.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 31

q: In a Texas school crossing zone with the reduced limit in effect, a driver 18 or older may:
a: Hold a phone to talk if the call is short
b: Use a hands-free device, or a phone when stopped
c: Read a text, but not send one
d: Use a handheld phone if no children are present
exp: Handheld use is banned in an active school crossing zone unless the car is stopped; hands-free use is allowed for adults.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.425, 545.4252; TxDOT statewide texting release

q: In a Texas construction or maintenance work zone, traffic fines double when:
d: Orange cones are in place, workers or not
exp: Fines double in construction zones where workers are present.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, pp. 36, 38

q: Driving around a barricade placed where water covers a Texas road is:
a: A ticket: up to $200, doubled if workers are present
b: A misdemeanor: up to $500, with no jail time
c: Legal if your truck or SUV sits high enough
d: A misdemeanor: up to $2,000 and 180 days in jail
exp: Ignoring a barricade at a flooded road is a Class B misdemeanor.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 38

q: In Texas, after stopping at a steady red light, which turn may you make if no sign forbids it?
b: A left turn onto any street
exp: Texas allows a right turn on a steady red after a stop, yielding to pedestrians and traffic.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 25; Tex. Transp. Code 544.007(d)

q: When may you turn left on a steady red light in Texas?
a: From any street onto a one-way street
b: From a one-way street onto another one-way street
c: From a two-way street onto a one-way street
d: From a two-way street onto another two-way street
exp: A left on red is allowed only when both streets are one-way, after a stop.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 25; Tex. Transp. Code 544.007(d)

q: Facing a steady red arrow in Texas, what should you do?
a: Stop, then turn after yielding, like a red light
b: Stop, then turn right after yielding, but not left
c: Stop and wait for a green signal before turning
d: Slow down and turn if no one is coming
exp: The Texas turn on red law covers only a steady red light; a red arrow means do not make that turn.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 544.007

q: A flashing yellow arrow for a left turn means:
a: Turn left; oncoming traffic must stop for you
b: Stop, then wait for the green arrow to turn
c: Finish your turn; the arrow is about to turn red
d: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic
exp: A flashing yellow arrow allows the turn, but oncoming traffic has the right-of-way.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 25

q: A Texas police car is stopped on the shoulder with lights flashing, on a road with two lanes in your direction. What does the law require?
a: Leave the lane next to it, or slow to 20 below the limit
b: Leave the lane next to it, or slow to 10 below the limit
c: Stay in your lane and slow by 5 mph
d: Stop behind the police car until it leaves
exp: On a road with two or more lanes your way, you must either vacate the lane closest to the stopped vehicle or slow to 20 mph below the limit.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 4, p. 23; Ch. 8, p. 46; Tex. Transp. Code 545.157(b)

q: Under the Texas Move Over law, if you cannot change lanes and the limit is 60 mph, you must slow to:
exp: You must slow to 20 mph below the posted limit when it is 25 mph or more.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 4, p. 23; Ch. 8, p. 46

q: Which stopped vehicle with lights on is covered by the Texas Slow Down or Move Over law?
a: A disabled car with its hazards on
exp: The law covers emergency vehicles, tow trucks, utility vehicles and TxDOT or road work vehicles.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 8, p. 46

q: What is the fine for a first violation of the Texas Move Over law?
exp: A first offense is a misdemeanor with a fine of $500 to $1,250.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.157 as amended by HB 898 (88R)

q: A Texas school bus ahead of you is stopped with red lights flashing on a two-lane road. When may you go on?
a: When the bus moves, you are signaled on, or the lights stop
b: After the last child has reached the sidewalk
c: When the stop arm is folded, even if the red lights still flash
d: After the bus driver turns off the yellow lights
exp: You must stay stopped until one of those three things happens.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 4, p. 23; Tex. Transp. Code 545.066

q: On a Texas highway with separate roadways divided by a raised median, a school bus stops on the other roadway with red lights flashing. You must:
a: Stop until the lights go off
b: Continue with care; you are not required to stop
d: Stop, then go once the children are on the bus
exp: Drivers on a separate roadway need not stop.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.066

q: In Texas, does a center left turn lane create separate roadways for school bus stopping rules?
b: Yes, if the bus is on the far side of the turn lane
c: No, traffic in both directions must stop
exp: Roadways separated only by a left turn lane are not separate roadways.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.066(f)

q: What is the fine for a first offense of illegally passing a stopped school bus in Texas?
exp: A first conviction carries a fine of $500 to $1,250.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 4, p. 23; Tex. Transp. Code 545.066

q: In Texas, for how far must you signal continuously before turning?
exp: Texas requires a continuous signal for at least 100 feet before turning.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 6, pp. 38 to 39

q: A sign at a Texas intersection shows a U-shaped arrow with a red slash. You should:
a: Make a U-turn only after stopping
d: Make a U-turn only from the left lane
exp: The sign prohibits U-turns at that intersection.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 30

q: What is the Texas speed limit in an urban district when no sign is posted?
exp: The prima facie limit in an urban district is 30 mph.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 8, p. 46

q: What is the Texas speed limit in an alley?
exp: The prima facie speed limit in an alley is 15 mph.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 8, p. 46

q: Outside a city, what is the Texas speed limit for a car on a numbered state or U.S. highway when no other limit is posted?
exp: Numbered highways outside an urban district have a 70 mph limit for passenger cars.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 8, p. 46

q: Outside a city, what is the Texas limit for a car on a road not numbered as a state or U.S. highway?
exp: Unnumbered highways outside an urban district have a 60 mph limit for passenger cars.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 8, p. 46

q: In good conditions above 30 mph, what following gap does the Texas handbook call for?
exp: Above 30 mph, keep a four-second gap in good conditions.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 8, p. 45

q: In good conditions at 30 mph or less, what is the minimum following gap in the Texas handbook?
exp: At 30 mph or less, the minimum is two seconds in good conditions.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 8, p. 45

q: How much following distance does the Texas handbook advise behind a motorcycle?
exp: Allow at least four to six seconds when following a motorcycle.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 9, p. 52

q: A Texas HOV preferential lane sign lists buses and carpools 6 a.m. to 9 a.m., Monday through Friday. A solo driver may use the lane:
c: During those hours, if traffic is light
exp: The restriction applies only during the posted hours.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 30

q: Where should you enter or leave a Texas HOV lane separated by a buffer or barrier?
exp: Enter and leave only where the signs and markings show an opening.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, pp. 30, 35

q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in Texas?
exp: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 7, p. 42

q: In Texas, you may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
exp: Parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection is prohibited.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 7, p. 42

q: In Texas, how close to a stop sign at the side of the road may you park?
exp: Do not park within 30 feet of a roadside stop sign, yield sign or signal.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 7, p. 42

q: In Texas, how far must you park from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?
exp: Do not park within 50 feet of the nearest rail.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 7, p. 42

q: On the opposite side of the street from a Texas fire station entrance, you may not park within:
exp: Parking across from a fire station entrance is banned within 75 feet.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 7, p. 42

q: When parallel parked on a two-way Texas road, your right wheels must be within how far of the curb?
exp: The right wheels must be within 18 inches of the curb or road edge.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 7, pp. 43 to 44

q: What is the fine for a first offense of parking in a Texas disability space without a plate or placard?
exp: The first offense is a misdemeanor with a fine of $500 to $750.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 7, p. 42

q: What minimum distance does Texas state law set for passing a bicycle?
b: 4 feet, or a full lane change
c: None set by state law; give a safe gap
d: 6 feet on roads posted over 35 mph
exp: Texas has no statewide passing distance, though some cities set one by ordinance.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 9 and 13; City of San Antonio Safe Passing Ordinance page

q: A cyclist rides in the middle of a narrow Texas traffic lane, too narrow to share side by side. The cyclist is:
b: Required to ride on the sidewalk
c: Required to move onto the shoulder when a car comes up behind
d: Allowed to use the full lane
exp: A cyclist may take the full lane when it is too narrow to share safely.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 9, p. 53; Ch. 13, p. 62

q: After a Texas crash with no injuries, if both cars can be driven safely, the drivers should:
a: Move the cars off the main lanes to a safe nearby spot
b: Leave the cars where they stopped until police arrive
c: Stay in the cars with hazard lights on until a tow truck arrives
d: Leave once they have each other's phone numbers
exp: Drivable vehicles must be moved off main lanes to a safe location such as a frontage road or cross street.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 11, p. 59

q: You hit an unattended parked car in Texas and cannot find the owner. What must you do?
a: Drive away if the damage is under $500
b: Securely attach a note with your name and address
c: Wait 30 minutes for the owner, then drive away
d: Call your insurer, who will contact the owner
exp: You must find the owner or securely attach a notice with your information.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 11, p. 60

q: In Texas, when should you notify police about a crash?
a: When damage is over $1,000, or when a driver has no insurance card
b: After every crash, even one with only minor scrapes
c: When someone is hurt, a car cannot move, or a driver flees or is drunk
d: When you were at fault, or when the other driver asks you to call
exp: Notify law enforcement as soon as possible in each of those cases.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 11, p. 59

q: In Texas, within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you switch to low beams?
exp: Use low beams within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 9, p. 47

q: In Texas, within how many feet of a vehicle you are following must you use low beams?
exp: Use low beams when following within 300 feet of another vehicle.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 9, p. 47

q: When must Texas drivers have headlights on?
b: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or when visibility is under 1,000 feet
c: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or when you cannot see 500 feet ahead
d: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
exp: Headlights are required in those hours and whenever people or vehicles cannot be seen clearly at 1,000 feet.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 9, p. 47

q: What is the legal BAC limit for a Texas driver 21 or older?
exp: A driver 21 or older is legally intoxicated at a BAC of 0.08 or more.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, pp. 55, 58

q: What amount of alcohol is illegal for a Texas driver under 21?
exp: Under zero tolerance, any detectable alcohol while driving is an offense for a minor.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 56

q: A Texas driver under 21 drives with a small, detectable amount of alcohol, below 0.08. What is the offense?
a: Driving Under the Influence by a Minor
b: No offense, since it is below 0.08
d: A DWI, the same as for adults
exp: Any detectable amount is the criminal offense of DUI by a Minor.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 56

q: An adult arrested for DWI in Texas refuses a breath or blood test for the first time. The license is suspended for:
exp: A first refusal suspends the license for 180 days.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 58

q: An adult in Texas takes the test after a DWI arrest and shows 0.08 or more for the first time. The license suspension is:
exp: A first test result of 0.08 or more brings a 90 day suspension, up to a year for repeats.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 58

q: A Texas minor gives a specimen showing a detectable amount of alcohol for the first time. The license is suspended for:
exp: A first failure by a minor brings a 60 day suspension.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 57

q: What is the maximum fine for a first DWI conviction in Texas?
exp: A first DWI carries a fine of up to $2,000 plus 72 hours to 180 days in jail.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 58

q: For a first DWI in Texas, the jail term ranges from:
exp: A first DWI is punished by 72 hours to 180 days in jail.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 58

q: In Texas, an open container of alcohol in a vehicle's passenger area on a public road is:
b: Legal if the vehicle is stopped
c: Illegal even if the vehicle is parked
d: Legal if the container is in a bag
exp: Possessing an open container in the passenger area is illegal whether the vehicle is moving, stopped or parked.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 56

q: What is the maximum fine for an open container violation in Texas?
exp: An open container conviction carries a fine of up to $500.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 56

q: Texas bans all drivers from which phone activity while driving?
a: Reading, writing or sending electronic messages
b: Talking on the phone through a hands-free system
c: Using GPS navigation on a mounted phone
d: Making a call in an emergency
exp: The statewide law bans electronic messaging while driving, with exceptions for emergencies and a stopped vehicle.
src: TxDOT statewide texting release; Tex. Transp. Code 545.4251

q: What is the most a first-time offender can be fined for texting while driving in Texas?
exp: A first offense carries a fine of up to $99; repeat offenses up to $200.
src: TxDOT statewide texting release

q: A Texas driver age 17 wants to take a call using a hands-free system. This is:
b: Legal if the call is short
d: Legal with a passenger in the car
exp: Drivers under 18 may not use a wireless device, even hands-free, except in an emergency.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 3; Ch. 9, p. 48

q: Who must wear a seat belt in a Texas passenger vehicle?
a: The driver and front seat passengers
c: Front seat riders and anyone under 18
d: Everyone in the vehicle, in every seat
exp: All occupants, regardless of age or seat, must be belted where belts are installed.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 14, p. 64

q: A Texas driver carries a 14-year-old passenger who is not belted. Who can be fined, and how much?
exp: The fine for a passenger under 17 riding unbelted is assessed to the driver; passengers are fined themselves only from age 15.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 14, p. 64

q: What is the fine for a Texas driver who is not wearing a seat belt?
exp: Driving without a safety belt carries a fine of $25 to $50.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 14, p. 64

q: In Texas, a child under 8 must ride in a child safety seat unless the child is taller than:
exp: Children under 8 need a child passenger safety seat unless taller than 4 feet 9 inches.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 14, p. 64; Tex. Transp. Code 545.412

q: What is the fine range for a Texas child safety seat violation?
exp: The offense is a misdemeanor with a fine of $25 to $250.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.412

q: May a 12-year-old ride in the open bed of a pickup truck on a Texas street?
a: No, except in cases such as a parade
b: Yes, if the truck goes under 30 mph
c: Yes, if an adult rides in the bed too
d: Yes, if the tailgate is closed
exp: Children under 18 may not ride in an open bed, with limited defenses such as parades and emergencies.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 14, p. 64

q: What does Texas require of most non-commercial cars instead of a yearly safety inspection?
a: A safety inspection every two years
c: A $25 safety check at any garage
d: An emissions test in every county
exp: Since safety inspections ended for non-commercial vehicles, owners pay a $7.50 fee at registration.
src: DPS news release, Vehicle Safety Inspection Changes

q: What minimum liability insurance must a Texas driver carry?
exp: Texas minimum liability coverage is 30/60/25: $30,000 per injured person, $60,000 per crash for injuries and $25,000 for property damage.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 3, p. 18

q: Within how many days must you register a newly bought vehicle in Texas?
exp: An owner must register a newly purchased vehicle within 30 days.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 2, p. 16

q: What is the minimum tire tread depth for a Texas vehicle?
exp: Tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 2, p. 15

q: On the Texas road test, about how far are you asked to back up straight?
exp: The backing exercise covers about 60 feet at a slow speed.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 8

q: Which of these causes an automatic fail on the Texas road test?
a: Asking the examiner to repeat an instruction
b: Using a backup camera to parallel park
d: Stopping behind the stop line, then creeping forward to see
exp: Violating the law, refusing instructions, dangerous driving or a crash all fail the exam.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 8

q: What must you show for the vehicle you use on a Texas road test?
a: The title and a recent safety inspection
b: The title and the owner's driver license
c: Nothing; the examiner checks it online
d: Current registration and proof of insurance
exp: DPS requires current registration and insurance for the test vehicle.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 8; dps.texas.gov, Texas Provisional License as a Teen

q: An emergency vehicle with its siren on comes up behind you on a Texas one-way street. Where should you pull over?
a: To the right edge, clear of any intersection
b: To whichever edge is closer, left or right
c: To the left edge, since the street is one-way
d: Stop in your lane right where you are
exp: Texas law sends you to the right-hand edge or curb, clear of any intersection, and gives no different rule for one-way streets.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.156; TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 4, p. 22

q: In Texas, how close may you follow a fire truck answering an alarm?
exp: Unless on official business, you may not follow within 500 feet of a fire truck answering an alarm or an ambulance with red lights flashing.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.407; TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 4, p. 22

q: A fire truck has stopped on a Texas street to answer an alarm. What does the law say about that block?
a: You may park on it if you stay 50 feet from the truck
b: You may drive through it at 10 mph
c: You may not drive or park on it
d: You may use it once the siren is off
exp: Texas bars driving into or parking on the block where a fire truck has stopped to answer an alarm.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.407(a); TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 4, p. 22

q: In Texas, when does the nighttime headlight rule begin each evening?
exp: Headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 541.401, 547.302; TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 9, p. 47

q: It is midday in heavy rain on a Texas highway, and you cannot clearly see cars 1,000 feet ahead. What does the law require?
exp: Texas requires headlights whenever people or vehicles cannot be seen clearly at 1,000 feet, at any time of day.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 547.302(a); TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 9, p. 47

q: You must park on an unlit Texas highway at night. What lights should you leave on?
d: No lights, to save the battery
exp: The Texas handbook says to leave parking lights or low beam headlights on when parked on an unlighted highway at night.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 9, p. 47

q: During a Texas traffic stop, your insurance card is in the glove box. What should you do before reaching for it?
a: Get it out quickly before the officer reaches the window
b: Step out of the car and hand it over at the trunk
c: Tell the officer where it is, then follow directions
d: Wait until the officer leaves, then mail a copy
exp: The Texas handbook says to tell the officer where your license or insurance is before you reach for it, then follow the officer's directions.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 14, p. 65

q: A car with flashing lights signals you to stop on a dark Texas road, and you are not sure it is a real police car. What does the Texas handbook suggest?
a: Keep driving at the limit until you get home
b: Stop right away in the travel lane and get out
c: Ignore it until you reach the next town
d: Turn on your hazards, drive slowly and call 911
exp: You may turn on your hazard lights, drive slowly below the limit, call 911 and stop in a well-lit, busy place.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 14, p. 65

q: During a Texas traffic stop, which must a driver do when the officer asks?
b: Answer every question about the trip
c: Let the officer search the car
d: Get out and stand behind the car
exp: Drivers must show a driver license when an officer asks. You may decline to answer questions or refuse consent to a search.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 14, pp. 65 to 66

q: A 19-year-old in Texas is convicted for the first time of possessing alcohol. No car was involved. What happens to the license?
a: Nothing, since no car was involved
exp: A first non-driving alcohol offense by a minor brings a fine up to $500, community service, an alcohol awareness course and a 30-day suspension.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 56, Table 26

q: A 20-year-old shows a fake ID to buy beer at a Texas store. Which is true?
a: It is legal if the store accepts the ID
b: It is a crime, but the license is not affected
c: It is a crime that can cost the license
d: The clerk is charged, but not the buyer
exp: Minors may not falsely state they are 21 or show a document saying so to buy alcohol; misrepresentation of age leads to a license suspension.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 11; Ch. 10, p. 56

q: For a second non-driving alcohol offense by a Texas minor, how long is the license suspended?
exp: A second offense brings a 60-day suspension, a fine up to $500 and 20 to 40 hours of community service.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 10, p. 56, Table 26

q: How does Texas track a driver's moving violations?
a: By counting convictions; Texas has no point system
b: With 2 points per ticket and a suspension at 12 points
c: With points that drop off after 6 months
d: With points used only for drivers over 21
exp: DPS stopped assessing driver points when the Driver Responsibility Program ended. Repeated convictions can still bring a suspension.
src: dps.texas.gov, Driver Responsibility Program Surcharge Repeal FAQs; Tex. Transp. Code 521.292

q: Texas DPS may suspend a driver as a habitual violator after how many moving violation convictions within 12 months?
exp: A habitual violator has 4 or more moving violation convictions in 12 months, or 7 or more in 24 months.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 521.292(b); TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 1, p. 11

q: What is the fine for a first conviction of driving without proof of liability insurance in Texas?
exp: A first conviction costs $175 to $350; later convictions bring $350 to $1,000, a suspension and possible impoundment.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 3, p. 18, Table 13

q: In a Texas work zone, what is the fine for ignoring a warning sign or driving around a barricade?
a: Up to $100, doubled when workers are present
b: Up to $200, the same whether or not workers are present
c: Up to $2,000 and up to 180 days in jail
d: Up to $200, doubled when workers are present
exp: Ignoring a work zone warning sign or driving around a barricade costs up to $200, and the fine doubles when workers are present. The $2,000 and 180-day penalty is for driving around a barricade where water covers the road.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, pp. 36, 38

q: A Texas School Zone sign has yellow lights on it. When does its lower speed limit apply?
a: While the lights flash, or during posted hours
b: When you can see children near the road or crosswalk
c: All day, on any day school is in session
d: From 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. on school days
exp: The school zone limit applies while the yellow lights flash or during the times shown on the sign.
src: TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 31

q: In a Texas school crossing zone while the lower speed limit is in effect, when may a driver use a handheld phone?
a: Any time, if the call is short
b: Only when stopped or in an emergency
c: Only to read a text, not to send one
d: Only if the driver is 18 or older
exp: Handheld phone use is banned in an active school crossing zone unless the car is stopped or there is an emergency.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.425; TX Driver Handbook (DL-7, rev. Jan 2026), Ch. 5, p. 31

q: Texas bans turning around on a curve or near a hilltop if other drivers cannot see your car from how far away?
exp: You may not turn around on a curve or near the crest of a grade where drivers from either direction cannot see the car within 500 feet.
src: Tex. Transp. Code 545.102
